content: The development of monthly Voluntary Medical Male Circumcision (VMMC) plans involved active collaboration with community leaders and education authorities. Quality supportive supervisory visits were conducted, and efforts were made to integrate VMMC planning and implementation with other health initiatives, such as girls’ HPV vaccination campaigns. Enhanced partnerships between international non-governmental organizations (NGOs) and the Ministry of Health and Child Care (MoHCC) significantly improved service delivery. Local clinicians were actively involved in providing services, fostering local ownership and engagement. A dedicated team offered VMMC services at night, referred to as moonlight services, targeting male members of religious sects that typically avoid biomedical interventions. These procedures were performed and followed up by Apostolic clinicians from a different province. A WhatsApp platform was established to enable service delivery teams across the province to share their outputs, experiences, challenges, and ideas. Additionally, the international NGO introduced a new role, the District Field Officer, who resides in the district and acts as a liaison among various district stakeholders. Engagement with schools was strengthened, with over 450 teachers responsible for health issues identified and trained in VMMC mobilization in March 2018. Community leaders, including political, religious (Muslim and Apostolic), and traditional leaders, were trained to deliver basic VMMC messaging and to use public gatherings as platforms to promote the program. Starting in May 2018, three districts began exceeding their monthly reportable targets, achieving 102%, 138%, 123%, 134%, and 130% of their goals in May, June, July, August, and September, respectively. Lessons Learned: 1. Engaging and involving key stakeholders is critical for creating demand for VMMC services and ensuring effective service delivery. 2.
